title: The first moment of cubic Gauss sums
author: Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic)
description: The unconditional proof, after OpenAI's 2026 manuscript, of Patterson's first-moment conjecture: the normalized cubic Gauss sums over the primary primes of Z[omega] of norm at most X add up to (6/5) c_* X^(5/6)/log X + o(X^(5/6)/log X), with c_* = (2 pi)^(2/3)/(3 Gamma(2/3)); every fixed nontrivial angular mode cancels, which settles the moments of the powers G^k with k not divisible by 3. Eisenstein integers, cubic residue symbols and the cube of a Gauss sum; large sieves for cubic characters; the level Voronoi formula and Type I sums; character moments at two exceptional configurations; corrected dispersion; an exact decomposition of the prime sum; the sharp cutoff.
prerequisites: power residue symbols, the cubic reciprocity law and ideal reciprocity with conductors (course Class field theory, lessons Power residue symbols and reciprocity laws; Ray class fields, conductors and ideal reciprocity)
Gauss sums of Dirichlet characters and the prime number theorem for arithmetic progressions (course Dirichlet L-functions and primes in progressions, NT-DIRL-03 and NT-DIRL-09)
Mertens' estimates, the Gamma function and Stirling's formula, mean values of Dirichlet polynomials (course The Riemann zeta function, NT-ZETA-02, NT-ZETA-03, NT-ZETA-16)
Hecke characters and the functional equation of Hecke L-functions (course Adeles, ideles and Tate's thesis, NT-ADL-06 and NT-ADL-10)
Fourier inversion and Poisson summation on lattices (course Harmonic analysis on locally compact abelian groups)

open_obligations: N1 Heath-Brown's cubic large sieve (Heath-Brown, Kummer's conjecture for cubic Gauss sums, Israel J. Math. 120 (2000), Theorem 2; stated as Theorem 9.1 of Dunn-Radziwill, arXiv:2109.07463v3). Used in the lessons Large sieves for cubic characters (Theorem 4.1 and Lemma 4.2), The level formula and Type I sums, Character moments at two exceptional configurations, Corrected dispersion and An exact decomposition of the prime sum. Intended home: a lesson on the cubic large sieve placed before the lesson Large sieves for cubic characters.

N2 The level Voronoi formula of Dunn and Radziwill (arXiv:2109.07463v3, Proposition 5.3, with the dual coefficients of Proposition 5.2 and Patterson's cubic theta coefficients in Section 5.1). Used in the lesson The level formula and Type I sums (Theorem 2.1). Intended home: lessons on Kubota's cubic metaplectic forms and Patterson's cubic theta function.

N3 Prime number theorems for Hecke characters of Q(omega) with conductor at most a power of log x (Thorner-Zaman, arXiv:1803.02823v3, Theorem 1.4, for cubic characters; Kaneko-Thorner, arXiv:2203.09515v2, Theorem 1.2, with the zero-free region of Chen-Park-Swaminathan, arXiv:1506.09170v3, Lemma 2.1, for fixed angular order). Used in the lessons Large sieves for cubic characters (Theorem 6.4), An exact decomposition of the prime sum (Lemma 6.1) and Angular modes and powers of Gauss sums (Proposition 1.2). Intended home: lessons on zero-free regions for Hecke L-functions, after the course Dirichlet L-functions and primes in progressions.

Not used: Heath-Brown's mean-square estimate for the Dirichlet series of G(ru) (2000, Section 3, Lemma 3); the high-height Type I bound is derived from N2 instead (The level formula and Type I sums, Lemma 5.1 and Remark 5.3).
